title: The Last Five Overs: When Mumbai Indians Should Preserve or Spend Resources
dek: When should Mumbai Indians preserve resources in the last five overs and when should they spend them? Wickets in hand at the fifteenth over set the ceiling.
excerpt: Since 2024 Mumbai Indians have out-scored their opponents in the last five overs. League-wide, wickets in hand at the fifteenth over decide how fast the finish can be.

sections.heading: Five Overs, Two Ledgers
body: The last five overs are where most T20 matches are decided, and every team has two ledgers there: runs scored and runs conceded.

Since 2024 Mumbai Indians have scored {{ev:l5bat-team-e2}} an over in the death and conceded {{ev:l5bowl-team-e2}}, a net of {{ev:l5-net}} per over. The league scoring rate in that phase is {{ev:l5bat-league-e2}}.

sections.heading: Wickets in Hand Set the Ceiling
body: How fast a side can finish depends on what it has left. Across the league since 2022, sides with three or fewer wickets down after fifteen overs scored {{ev:l5-fresh}} an over in the death; sides six or more down scored {{ev:l5-deep}}.
That is the price of spending wickets earlier: a slower finish.

sections.heading: Preserve or Spend
body: With the bat, the rule follows from the table: protect wickets through the middle overs when the finishers are strong, because they convert wickets in hand into runs at the death.
With the ball, spend the best death bowler's overs where the batting side has most wickets in hand, since that is where the scoring ceiling is highest.

sections.heading: Correlation and Collapse
body: Sides six down after fifteen overs are often the weaker batting sides, so part of the slower finish reflects quality rather than state. The table describes outcomes, not the effect of a single decision.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Bank Wickets, Then Cash Them
body: Mumbai Indians have won the death-overs ledger since 2024. The league evidence says wickets in hand at the fifteenth over are what turn a finish into a big one.
Batting plans should protect wickets until the fifteenth over; bowling plans should target that same window.
